title: Cedar Grove Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Cedar Grove Health onboarding to Redwood. Discussed scope, timelines, security requirements (SAML, SOC2, KMS), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), performance targets, pilot evaluation plan, and next steps including security doc share, demo environment, and pilot runbook.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and security pack (Hannah)
SE to provision demo tenant and invite Cedar Grove (Diego)
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and compliance contact (Tom)
Schedule pilot kickoff for week of Apr 11
action_items: Hannah Kim: Share SOC2 report and security pack by 2027-04-01
Diego Alvarez: Stand up demo tenant and provide access by 2027-04-04
Tom Reynolds: Share sample traffic/sequence length distribution and SLO targets by 2027-04-05
Priya Singh: Confirm list of stakeholders and procurement timeline by 2027-04-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Hannah Kim (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (Cedar Grove), Priya Singh, Ethan Cole, Lara Mitchell, Sam Ortiz

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood. Uh, quick round of intros?
[00:08] Tom (Cedar Grove): Yeah Tom here, Head of Platform at Cedar Grove. We'll be driving integration.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, engineering manager, I'll own the infra side.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan, DevOps, networking stuff.
[00:20] Maya: Great, and Diego SE from Redwood, Hannah our CSM.
[00:25] Diego (SE): Hi folks, hi, glad to be here.
[00:28] Hannah (CSM): Quick note, we'll put the slides and security pack in the follow-up.

[02:05] Maya: Objective for this call is to align on kickoff plan, collect requirements, and agree next steps for the pilot. High level: sample traffic, compliance needs, success criteria, and timeline.

[03:10] Priya: On our side we need privacy and data residency - some PHI-ish data, so VPC option and KMS are must-haves.
[03:22] Lara (Security): Also SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. We'll need SOC2 evidence and key management integration (we use AWS KMS).
[03:35] Hannah: Yep we support SAML, RBAC, audit logs; for KMS we can integrate customer-managed keys in our Private offering, for hosted we have encryption at rest with customer key options - I'll include specifics in the pack.

[05:00] Diego: On the technical side, curious about latency targets and expected throughput. What's your SLO?
[05:08] Tom: Target p95 latency under 400ms for short prompts (~512 tokens), and sustained 100 qps for embeddings and 20 concurrent generation requests. Cost is a factor, we want balance.
[05:22] Maya: Ok that's helpful. For that profile, Dedicated or Private deployment with reserved capacity makes sense to guarantee throughput. Hosted can work for initial eval but may require autoscaling.

[06:50] Ethan: On networking - will we need a VPN or just VPC peering? We use AWS in us-east-1.
[06:58] Diego: For Private deployments we support VPC peering or Transit Gateway. We can discuss a VPN as fallback. For hosted we also support private endpoints via VPC endpoints.

[08:30] Priya: Any limitations around model support? We're evaluating a few redwood curated models and also want to test a quantized variant for cost reasons.
[08:40] Diego: We onboard models and provide quantization profiles. For heavy throughput, int8 quantized runs are common. We'll advise on tradeoffs in quality vs cost - we can run A/B on the pilot.

[10:12] Tom: Security review pace is typical procurement blocker - can you share your SOC2 and pen test results?
[10:18] Hannah: Absolutely, we'll share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and our security whitepaper. Expect that in the follow-up.

[12:05] Maya: Let's map success criteria for pilot: 1) Latency within 400ms p95 on our workload, 2) No data leakage, verified by audit logs and controls, 3) Cost per 1k tokens below threshold - I think you said cost sensitivity - what's an acceptable number?
[12:24] Sam (Product): We don't have exact $/1k yet, we'd like Redwood's estimate and then compare.
[12:30] Maya: We'll include an estimated cost sheet based on your traffic profile.

[14:00] Diego: Can you share a sample of your production traffic distribution? seq lengths, concurrency, embedding vs generation ratio - that'll help design instance sizing and batching.
[14:10] Tom: Yep we'll share a week of anonymized logs, we can scrub PHI.

[15:40] Priya: On the authentication flow - we'd like SAML SSO for users and service principals for machine access. Is that supported?
[15:47] Hannah: Yes, SAML for UI access; service tokens for API with RBAC. We also have audit logging for all token ops.

[18:00] Ethan: Regarding private key management, can Redwood use our KMS for disk encryption?
[18:06] Diego: In Private deployments yes; Dedicated can also integrate with customer keys via our KMS connector. For hosted there are different patterns - we'll include details.

[20:05] Tom: For the pilot, we'd like to run both hosted and dedicated comparisons - small hosted workload for quick start, then a dedicated pilot to validate throughput/cost.
[20:18] Maya: That's a common approach; we'll propose a two-phase pilot: Phase 1 hosted proof-of-feasibility, Phase 2 dedicated perf/cost run.

[22:50] Priya: On rollout strategy - can Redwood do canary rollouts or automatic fallback if a model regresses?
[22:58] Diego: Yes, our console supports canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model variants or cheaper tiers. We'll show this in the demo.

[25:10] Sam: Any references for similar healthcare customers?
[25:16] Hannah: We have a few redacted case studies; will share with security pack.

[27:30] Maya: Procurement questions - are there standard enterprise contract terms, SLAs?
[27:38] Hannah: Yes, we have SLA options for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we have standard uptime targets. Sales will follow up on contracts; I'll include pricing ranges.

[30:00] Diego: For benchmarking, we typically run a synthetic load plus your sample traces. We'll want to coordinate time window for test to avoid production impact.
[30:10] Tom: We'll do a backup environment.

[32:40] Priya: What's the typical timeline from kickoff to pilot?
[32:46] Maya: Usually 2-4 weeks for Phase 1 hosted plus demo and security review, then 3-6 weeks for a dedicated pilot depending on networking and procurement. So expecting pilot kickoff mid-April sounds reasonable.

[35:00] Lara: A note on audit - we will request retention windows for logs and log export to our SIEM. Is that available?
[35:09] Diego: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or streamed to your SIEM; retention is configurable in Private and Dedicated.

[37:50] Ethan: Any gotchas on VPC peering with our existing Transit Gateway?
[37:57] Diego: Not usually; we'll work with your network team on routes, security groups, and NAT configs. We'll provide a network runbook.

[40:20] Sam: For evaluation, we want to test a quantized model for cost and a full-precision for quality checks.
[40:28] Diego: We'll run head-to-head with your prompts. Note that quantization may slightly change outputs; we'll track regression metrics in the evals dashboard.

[42:55] Maya: Okay let's recap actions and owners - Hannah will send SOC2/docs, Diego will stand up demo tenant, Tom will provide traffic profile, Priya will confirm infra stakeholders, and Maya will share pilot runbook and cost estimate.

[43:12] Tom: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[43:18] Maya: No blockers; just need your artifacts. Procurement might take time, but we'll support with docs.

[45:00] Priya: On metrics - can we get latency breakdown by token and breakdown of cost per token per model?
[45:08] Diego: Yes our console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and model-level dashboards. We'll add sample screenshots.

[47:00] Hannah: I'll also include onboarding checklist and suggested pilot timeline in the follow-up.

[50:10] Maya: Any final questions?
[50:20] Ethan: One last one - are there SLA credits for latency breaches?
[50:26] Hannah: SLA credits are defined for uptime; latency SLOs are part of Dedicated contract discussions. We'll include options.

[52:40] Sam: Competitors - we've had calls with Anthropic and looked into OpenAI and Bedrock. How does Redwood differentiate on ops?
[52:49] Maya: Our focus is unified runtime and production controls: transparent benchmarks, deployment policy, caching, batching, and cost controls. We'll provide a comparison doc.

[55:00] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the security pack and demo access by next week.
[55:08] Tom: Appreciate it.
[55:12] Priya: Thanks all.

[60:00] End of recording.
